messages:
Carla R: Quick playbook idea for per-region ephemeral auth onboarding (short, actionable). Posting so we can iterate.
Carla R: Goal: roll tenants to ephemeral mTLS client certs with operator automation; preserve a regional shared endpoint as fallback. Start with non-prod tenants in a single region.
Alice M: Two operational constraints: 1) some customers need preserved src IP, 2) DNS/client caching will bite us. We need documented SNAT behavior and low TTL during cutovers.
Brian W: Cost note: per-tenant peering keeps srcip but adds VPC attachments and route entries. Recommend gating per-tenant peering behind an enterprise opt-in.
Matt K: Air-gapped/install notes: support offline bootstrap via CSR upload. Allow longer TTL (24h) for offline certs and manual rotation instructions.
Carla R: Minimal operator API: /bootstrap -> token, /certs -> create/renew/revoke. Operator should emit handshake traces (tenant_id + trace_id).
Jen S: Rollout steps:
  1) Observe-only mode + synthetic traffic for 1 week
  2) Canary: 8 non-prod tenants in one region
  3) Gradual region ramp nightly windows
  4) Enable proxy-level auto-fallback on handshake errors (10m) + manual Console override
sre-bot: Draft alerts: handshake.error_rate >1% (5m); cert_renew.failures; route_churn.high
Alice M: UX: Console must show auth mode (shared | per-tenant), cert expiry, last handshake, and a force-fallback button.
Brian W: I'll run a cost delta table for peering vs shared endpoint by Tue. We should recommend per-tenant peering only for higher SLA tiers.
Matt K: I'll own offline docs + agent compatibility matrix. Agents must support auto-renew and a short fail-open window.
Carla R: I'll write the operator PR and the migration runbook after we collect feedback. If no objections in 24h I'll convert this thread into the RFC follow-up.
